title: The proof-sequence test permits a line to justify itself.
details:
[Smith, *An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems*](https://logicmatters.net/igt/pdfs/GodelBookLM.pdf),
second edition, Logic Matters corrected reprint August 2020, §20.4(a), p. 150
(PDF p. 164). Checked against the rendered page on 2026-10-19. Type: unsound
proof-checking definition.

In the displayed `Proofseq`, the modus-ponens premise indices may equal the
index of the line being checked. Start with a genuine proof of `A → A`, then
append `A`. The proposed check accepts the new line using the earlier
implication and the new line itself as its antecedent. In particular it accepts
a purported proof of contradiction. Replace both premise bounds by **strictly
earlier indices**; make the analogous strict-bound correction in the
universal-generalization clause. The intended proof-system theorem is valid
with this repair. The corpus instead checks strictly smaller child proof trees
and explicitly illustrates the circular-checking error in
[coding formal proofs](entries/coding-formal-proofs/entry.html#check-every-line).
